# Serīsakapetavatthu (Pv 37)

**ID:** Pv 37
**Section:** Petavatthu (pv)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Serīsakapetavatthu
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0507m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Serīsakapetavatthu* (Pv 37) is a narrative poem preserved in the *Petavatthu* of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya. The story concerns a *deva* (god) who encounters a group of merchants stranded and lost in the desert, instructing them on the karmic fruition of wholesome deeds and the importance of upholding ethical precepts. In a thematic analysis of Buddhist resolve (*adhiṭṭhāna*), the text is cited for its use of the verbal imperative *adhiṭṭhahātha* in the admonition *dhammānuyogañca adhiṭṭhahātha* ("resolutely determine on the practice of the Dhamma") [Lim Hwee San 2009].

A full parallel to the text exists in the *Vimānavatthu* as the *Serīsakavimānavatthu* (Vv 84).

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Full parallels: Vv 84 Serīsakavimānavatthu
- Mentioned in: Ja 524 Saṅkhapālajātaka; Ja 546 Vidhurajātaka
